To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the content of machine-generated summaries can be automatically assessed using a model derived from a wise crowd, and that the resulting scores correlate with human judgments of main ideas.

a highly reliable content assessment model can be derived automatically from summaries written by a small group of proficient writers, and that the resulting scores are correlated with a manual educational rubric.
a wise-crowd assessment method that is derived from summaries produced by an independent group is a reliable and interpretable method for assessing the content of student summaries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a content model that is derived from summaries of a source text, and is used to assess the content of a new summary.
the development of a reliable automated assessment of content that can be used in educational intervention studies.
developing automated methods to evaluate content quality and coverage, which are essential for evaluating educational interventions that address reading and language skills.

automated methods based on the wise crowd approach to content modeling provide an alternative to the labor-intensive development and application of rubrics for assessing content quality.
the wise-crowding content assessment method is highly reliable and can be automated.
we have developed a reliable automated content assessment method that can be applied to any text, and that is useful for educational intervention studies, and other applications.

the wise-crowds approach is a reliable, efficient, and interpretable method for content assessment that can be automated.
the wise-crowds content assessment model is a useful tool for evaluating machine-generated summaries and that it can be used to assess the quality of student writing.
the automated wise-crowd methods are as reliable as the main ideas rubrics, and have several advantages.

automated content assessment can be a useful and efficient tool for educational studies.
a content assessment method developed for machine-generated summaries can be applied to educational rubrics.
